title: Shuffled diary, frozen answer key
allegory: DQN is like a student who swaps a giant table of move scores for a trained gut feeling, studies from a shuffled diary of past moments, and marks each guess against an answer key photocopied from their older self that is only refreshed now and then, so the key holds still while they learn.
map: a gut feeling that scores every move in any situation
the Q-network: state in, one Q-value per action out
a diary of past moments, read back in shuffled order
the replay buffer: random minibatches of stored transitions
an answer key copied from your older self, refreshed only now and then
the target network θ⁻, synced every N steps
marking a guess against the reward plus the key's best next score
the TD target r + γ·max_a Q_target(s', a)
where_else: Critics in actor-critic and PPO: networks trained on bootstrapped targets, with the same stability worries
Self-training methods that learn from a slowly updated copy of the model, the same idea as a target network
Shuffling training data anywhere, to break the correlation between consecutive samples

hamming.what: Q-learning with a neural network in place of the table, kept stable by training on shuffled past experience and a periodically frozen copy of itself.
hamming.when: When states are too many or too rich for a table, such as raw game frames, but the actions are a small discrete set.
hamming.why: A network generalises to states it has never seen, and the replay buffer and target network stop it chasing its own moving predictions.
